newsitem.title: UK: Blair accepts victory, says new dawn in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Blair accepts victory, says new dawn in Britain.

text.p: Labour leader Tony Blair, Britain's new prime minister, said on Friday a new dawn had broken following his party's election landslide.

"A new dawn has broken and it is wonderful. I have always said that if we had the courage to change we would do it and we have done it," Blair told cheering supporters. "The British people have put their trust in us and it is a moving and humbling experience."
"We represent the whole of the nation and we will govern the whole of the nation, every single part of it," Blair said.

"This vote tonight has been a vote for a new era of politics in Britain so that we can put behind us the battles of this century and address the challenges of the new century." "Today on the eve of this new millennium the British people have ushered in this new era of politics," Blair said.

"We are now the people's party, the party of the many not the few. I believed in Britain and tonight the people of Britain are united behind New Labour." Labour are heading for a majority of 183 in the 659-seat parliament, according to BBC projections.
